brief: JPMorgan morning briefing. Escalating US and Iran strikes over the weekend push oil higher, and Reuters reports the US blockade has cut off Tehran's main revenue source even as more energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. APAC equities rose on a tech, AI and semis rebound tied to Astra / GPT-6 compute demand, EU futures were marginally lower, and US markets were closed. In FX, expected Japanese policy adjustment drove +4-sigma USD/JPY put demand. Meera stays constructive USD because the currency still undershoots rates and Fed re-pricing, and advises against the debasement narrative after the Treasury buyback announcement, consistent with the call to take tactical profit on gold with intent to re-enter. Growth risks skew above Econ's 2.6%ar 2H26 forecast with August PMI tracking 3.1%ar, payrolls confirm labour demand, so Fed speakers make this week's CPI the decisive input for the next FOMC. Consensus and Econ expect a 25bp ECB hike. The desk is tactically cautious on global equities, prefers US and Asia to Europe, holds supercycle-theme longs hedged with momentum options, is high conviction short EU chemicals and Asian consumer electronics, and is bullish EM through country-relative trades. Positioning shows hedge fund re-grossing at +1.3z.
